findings.affected_requirement: FR-014 and FR-061 eight-call navigation ceiling; AD-5 durable eight-attempt budget across the one Worker retry; navigate-code contract lines 87-94; strict-result-submission contract lines 9 and 51; no budget bypass across retry or restart
findings.evidence: The plan says the durable navigation budget is shared across the one retry (plan.md:25,196-198), and the navigation contract requires at most eight invocation attempts across all retries with no ninth attempt (contracts/navigate-code-contract.md:87-94). AD-21 instead makes a Guid.Empty/no-receipt callback consume only an execution-local slot without advancing ToolAttemptCount or the durable ordinal, then reconstructs both counters on retry solely from the unchanged store-provided RemainingNavigationBudget (plan.md:290; contracts/deepseek-strict-result-submission.md:51; quickstart.md:92-96). Therefore k no-receipt callbacks in attempt one can disappear after a JobTransient failure or process restart, and attempt two can receive the same durable remaining slot count and execute k additional callbacks beyond the stated job-wide eight-attempt ceiling. The requested retry-reconstruction tests (plan.md:351,383,457,533) do not define or detect this cross-attempt bypass; as written they can enshrine it.
findings.correction_outcome: Define one exact fail-closed authority for no-receipt callback consumption across an eligible durable retry and restart while preserving the required rule that Guid.Empty does not advance the durable receipt ordinal. Without adding a migration or new durable ledger, specify whether such a callback makes later Worker retry ineligible, conservatively reduces retry callback capacity from an existing durable fact, or uses another existing persisted authority; reconcile plan, research, data model, quickstart, strict-submission, navigate, and runtime contracts. Add behavioral RED proving the total released navigate_code callbacks across attempt one, restart, and attempt two never exceed eight, including multiple no-receipt calls followed by receipt-bearing siblings and later failure/retry. Do not regenerate tasks until this hidden budget decision is closed.

summary: REVISE. AD-21/R-22 otherwise provides a feasible pinned Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.6.0 whole-turn preflight seam below FICC; atomically rejects unknown, mixed, multi-submit, post-submit, malformed-ID, and over-budget batches before callbacks; executes accepted all-navigation batches serially in provider order; preserves complete reasoning, content, calls, and matching results; measures inactivity from nonzero raw reads while keeping the 25-minute absolute cap and 30-minute lease fixed; rejects ignored thinking sampling fields before send; keeps tool_choice, parallel_tool_calls, and response_format absent; closes the 401/402/403, 400/422, and 408/429/5xx taxonomy; makes no zero-retention claim; and adds no migration, dependency, manual provider loop, sibling-client behavior, host/system change, or Story 12.4/12.5 scope. One material budget contradiction prevents acceptance: Guid.Empty callbacks consume only transient slots, but retry reconstructs those slots solely from unchanged durable remaining budget, allowing no-receipt callbacks from a prior attempt to be forgotten and the job-wide eight-attempt ceiling to be exceeded across retry/restart. This is an earliest-owner plan defect because the accepted specification and existing navigation contract retain the bounded navigation ceiling, while the corrected design has not selected a durable or fail-closed reconstruction rule. The reviewed design-boundary identity is SHA-256 e66a023d10f95cbd73823aa85f69a24a4a531dbe3bc01a7cd8ea56138dfb360c over sorted path-tab-lowercase-hash rows for the seven corrected design artifacts. Prior plan-review-13 and definition-review-23 remain invalid; no task regeneration, implementation, qualification, lifecycle mutation, staging, commit, or Git-history action is authorized.
